fact: Afrique IT News reports the government invested in 1,275 km of fibre under PMICE and ordered Airtel and Moov Africa to connect to the national fibre network within seven days; no places or regions are named.
Minister Haliki Choua Mahamat said on 2026-10-09 that Chad has about 6,000 km of optical fibre, with a target of 14,000 km; the text does not say which regions it links.
Minister Haliki Choua Mahamat told the World Bank on 2026-09-15 that national fibre coverage is incomplete, with six provinces still not connected by fibre, and about 8,000 km still to deploy.

Citing the World Bank's June 2023 diagnostic, the national backbone has three axes (west, south, east), is almost wholly state-owned, operated by Sotel Tchad and Sudachad, and mainly links southern and eastern localities to N'Djamena.
Citing the World Bank's June 2023 diagnostic, two projects were under way: PMICE (1,200 km of fibre) and the Trans-Saharan backbone (550 km, Massaguet to N'Guigmi in Niger).

At a ministerial review on 19 May 2026 the PMICE coordinator reported 1,275 km of fibre deployed so far on the national backbone works, with Huawei as contractor under Gulf Consultancy supervision; the document does not say it is in service.
DCD reports the Ministry announced commencement on 20 December 2025 of PMICE Phase I (EUR 175.1m), which includes deploying 1,200 km of fibre optic cabling.

fact: Le N'Djam Post reports the minister inaugurated PMICE Phase I at Sarh (Moyen-Chari) on 20 December 2025; the project (EUR 175,106,916) includes a 1,200 km national fibre backbone, but the article does not say the backbone is lit.

Tchadinfos reports provisional acceptance of PMICE Phase I with inauguration of the Iriba-Doba fibre line at Sarh, a live IP-telephony test linking provincial governorates, and Safitel reporting 15 sites at 100 Gbit/s completed, within a new 1,200 km national backbone; capital connection and traffic in service not stated.

We Are Tech Africa reports the Chadian component of the Trans-Saharan Fiber Optic Backbone, assigned to the CGPS/LORYNE consortium and launched May 2023, was 32% complete on 6 March 2025 per the authorities, behind schedule.
